items.title: FCC signs off on SpaceX’s plan to put up to 1 million data center satellites into space
items.summary: The FCC has authorized SpaceX to deploy up to one million AI chip-equipped satellites for its "Starmind" initiative. This marks the first approval by the agency for a full constellation of AI satellites. SpaceX intends to use this constellation to power AI capabilities on Earth by capturing solar energy in space. The approval requires SpaceX to deploy at least one satellite by 2033 and reach the one million milestone by 2040. The FCC also deferred SpaceX's request regarding the disposal of satellites above 600km into "graveyard" orbits.

The approval allows SpaceX to use this constellation to generate power for artificial intelligence capabilities on Earth by capturing solar energy in space. The regulation mandates that SpaceX must deploy at least one satellite by the year 2033 and achieve the one million satellite milestone by 2040. items.title: Microsoft details how state-backed hackers use the ARTEX AI framework to automate cyberattacks
items.summary: State-backed hackers and criminal groups are using the ARTEX AI framework to automate cyberattacks via autonomous agents and existing tools like Metasploit. ARTEX operates at machine speed, autonomously distributing tasks and switching language models to evade detection, often leaving minimal response time for defenders. To counter this, Microsoft recommends deception tactics such as decoy systems and fake success signals to trick the AI into stopping attacks. The framework utilizes a multi-agent architecture to execute tasks from reconnaissance to data theft by leveraging existing security software. Defenders should implement these countermeasures alongside strict access controls and real-time isolation to manage the threat posed by adaptive AI agents.

items.title: How to Optimize NVFP4 Attention on NVIDIA RTX Blackwell Through Register Recycling
items.summary: NVFP4 enables 4-bit matrix multiplication on NVIDIA RTX Blackwell GPUs, offering higher throughput for attention workloads than BF16. An optimized kernel uses register recycling by splitting score tiles into two N64 slots, allowing subsequent operations to overlap with current tile computations. This scheduling reduces Tensor Core idle time and improves NVFP4 attention kernel latency by up to 1.64x on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell. Integrating this kernel into Reactor's serving stack resulted in end-to-end inference latency reductions of up to 15.34% across various world model workloads. The core optimization has been merged into the FlashInfer main branch for broader adoption.

items.title: sqlite3_rsync: Database Remote-Copy Tool For SQLite
items.summary: sqlite3_rsync is an SQLite tool designed for remote copying of databases over an SSH connection. It allows copying database snapshots to another machine without requiring a full local copy beforehand. The protocol works by exchanging cryptographic hashes of database pages to efficiently transfer only the differing content. It can also synchronize existing database copies without re-transmitting the entire data. This tool was added experimentally to SQLite and has been enhanced over time.

The protocol operates by exchanging cryptographic hashes of database pages to efficiently transfer only the differing content between the source and destination. items.title: How Looped Transformers Work and When They Save Memory
items.summary: Looped Transformers reuse the same Transformer blocks across multiple passes to update hidden states, separating stored model size from computation. This approach allows models to perform more work without acquiring new weights for every step. The system involves reusing weights and managing the flow of the hidden state through recurrent layers. Key considerations involve determining when an additional pass is worthwhile and measuring the trade-offs between parameters, compute, and reasoning quality. Adaptive depth and stopping rules are explored to optimize the efficiency of these looped models.

items.title: Mixture of Experts (MoE): History, Architecture & Modern LLMs
items.summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) originated from the 1991 Jacobs & Hinton paper, which proposed using a gating network to select an expert for each input case, fostering specialization. The key innovation in modern MoE is the Sparsely-Gated MoE layer, which achieves massive model capacity while maintaining computational efficiency through conditional computation. This approach allows models to scale to trillions of parameters by distributing tasks across multiple specialized experts. MoE has been integrated into Transformer architectures, leading to highly efficient Large Language Models like Mistral and Grok-1. This architecture is now driving the development of various state-of-the-art LLMs.

items.summary: Taste is defined more by what it rejects than what it admires, as having good taste involves recognizing what is intolerable rather than simply enjoying many things. AI will never develop true taste because developing it would require intolerance, which conflicts with the commercial need for AI to be universally agreeable to users. AI models are designed to accommodate the widest range of preferences, leading them to be cloyingly agreeable rather than discerning. Genuine taste involves the ability to withstand conflict and reject flattery, which is the antithesis of AI's current design. Therefore, for now, good taste remains a uniquely human attribute that serves as an insurmountable competitive advantage for users.

items.title: “Rewrite this as a new ordinance”: Inside the ChatGPT transcripts of a city manager
items.summary: A city manager in Kingsland, Georgia, used ChatGPT to generate a data center ordinance, which was later passed by the city council with minimal input from the manager. The AI was heavily involved in drafting various sections, including standards for water and noise, and created policies through interactive "offer-and-acceptance" loops. This practice raises concerns about the erosion of human judgment in critical government decisions, as AI can generate seemingly competent legal text quickly. Despite human review, the final ordinance contained inconsistencies, such as referencing non-existent zoning districts, and the process bypassed required public hearings. This case highlights the lack of oversight and established rules for using AI in local government policymaking.

items.title: The Agent Lake
items.summary: Agent Lake is a platform combining storage optimized for agent traces with intelligent compute to query, analyze, and learn from them for continuous agent improvement. It stores traces recording agent steps and outcomes, along with methods for generating those outcomes. Intelligent compute features like online evaluators and AI Search allow for finding high-signal traces and automating the agent improvement loop. Components such as Insights and Engine analyze traces to find problems and propose fixes, while SmithTune facilitates model fine-tuning based on agent trajectories. Ultimately, the agent lake provides the necessary foundation for organizations to effectively manage and improve the performance of large-scale AI agents.

items.title: Where scientists draw the line on AI agents
items.summary: Delegating research tasks to AI requires scientists to maintain responsibility for how work is accomplished, focusing on verifying methods, results, and safety constraints. Trust in AI for science hinges on validation, privacy, objectivity, accountability, and transparency, extending beyond mere accuracy. Scientists should guide which tasks agents perform and how performance is evaluated through benchmarks reflecting field-specific standards. Concerns also exist regarding the dilution of expertise and defining boundaries for intellectual contribution when using AI. Responsible development requires involving scientists in shaping the boundaries, safeguards, and evaluations for AI agents.

items.title: Verifiable Social Reasoning for LLM Assistants
items.summary: A framework based on multi-agent simulations is introduced to evaluate how well LLM assistants understand social situations from subjective user narratives. The framework involves a target agent with a hidden motive interacting with others, and the assistant must infer this motive based on the user's subsequent recounting. Evaluation reveals that relying on subjective user mediation complicates social reasoning and models are sensitive to user framing and narrative detail. Key findings highlight the "assistant-observer gap," where models perform better when observing objective events directly, and sensitivity to user framing. The framework aims to provide a systematic, empirical path toward developing reliable AI for everyday social reasoning.

The evaluation revealed that relying on subjective user mediation complicates social reasoning and models exhibit sensitivity to user framing and narrative detail. This framework involved setting up a target agent with a hidden motive interacting with others, requiring the assistant to infer that motive based on the user's subsequent recounting. Key findings indicated an assistant-observer gap, demonstrating that models perform more effectively when observing objective events directly and are highly sensitive to the framing provided by the user. This work establishes a systematic, empirical path toward developing reliable artificial intelligence for everyday social reasoning. The research points toward the necessity of integrating objective data streams to enhance the social understanding capabilities of future AI systems.

items.title: Evaluating Recent Model Releases on GDPx
items.summary: GDPx measures the most valuable domains for frontier intelligence, focusing on areas like chip design, cybersecurity, biology, and finance, rather than simple domain percentages. The benchmark's difficulty allows it to discriminate between model releases, with Opus 5.5 scoring only 12% on GDPx. OpenAI's models, specifically GPT-6.2 Astra, lead the overall leaderboard in raw intelligence across many domains. Fable 5.2 is strong in software engineering and finance but is significantly more expensive than 6.2 Astra. Domain-specific models are gaining relevance as providers restrict access to frontier knowledge.
